question: Why has war returned to Ethiopia's Tigray region?

lines.text: Overnight, Tigrayan forces took the airport in Mekelle. Ethiopia's Tigray war is back.
Ethiopian Airlines has suspended flights to Mekelle, Axum and Shire.
Fighting has spread into neighbouring Afar, up to Erebti, around 100 kilometres in, and into Amhara at Lalibela.
The last war here, from 2020 to 2022, killed about 600,000 people.
lines.note: African Union estimate, via Al Jazeera

lines.text: About a million people are still displaced from it.
Ethiopia's government accuses Eritrea of funding the fighters. Eritrea has denied similar claims before.
One analyst warns it could get very, very ugly without de-escalation.

scene.quote: could get very, very ugly if we don't see de-escalation

lines.text: A truce from 2022, broken in a single night. What stops it now?

sources.title: Ethiopian Airlines cancels flights to Tigray capital as fighters take over airport
Tigray rebels seize airport and clash with federal forces as fighting in Ethiopia reignites
Tigray forces launch offensive against Ethiopian government

caption: Tigrayan forces seized Mekelle airport overnight and fighting spread into Afar and Amhara. Ethiopian Airlines suspended flights to 3 Tigray airports. The last war killed about 600,000 people.
